Almost every Friday for more than a year, 14 students with autism and Down syndrome from Laredo's Mines Road area have been practicing basketball — running drills, shooting free throws, and learning defense — for an official game that has yet to come. They have never played anyone, simply because there is no other team like them.

The team is the Riverbanks, and behind it is Ana Aranda, a volunteer coach who is also a Community Relations Specialist with the United ISD Police Department — and a special-education parent herself, according to United ISD.

Aranda holds practice at George Washington Middle School, Ramirez Middle School, or Father McNaboe Park, patiently guiding players who struggle with loud noises while pushing others to play harder defense. She knows from personal experience how exclusion feels in the world of sports, the district reported, and decided she had to find a way to get a team going for these students.

She met with Washington Middle Principal David Guzman and Ramirez Middle Principal Juan Herrera, the campuses sent notices to parents — and parents started calling, thrilled their children would have something long-term, according to UISD.

Among the players: 7th-grader Anthony Martinez of Ramirez Middle School, who has autism and loves the sport, scoring routinely at practice. His parents, Alejandra Ramirez and Hector Martinez, say it was his first organized athletic activity — he has since joined soccer too. “We want to include our son in as many activities as we can,” Ramirez said, adding that at first he was scared to join, but once he saw everybody trying their best, he found what he could do.

Another player, Ramirez Middle student Leonardo Castaneda, has autism and needs a personal aide on the court — his older brother Luis, a United High School freshman on the 9th-grade white football team, fills that role. Their mother, Claudia L. Prado, cheers them both on from the sidelines.

The players, ages 11 to 16, have spent a year building fundamentals, confidence, and friendships. Now Aranda's plea is simple: she needs other parent volunteers across the district to form teams so games can finally begin. “We're ready to play. We just need one more team to get in there so we can start,” she said. Anyone interested can call her at 956-942-6777.

Sources: United ISD district news, Oct. 23, 2026.

title: A year of practices, no opponent yet: Laredo's Riverbanks basketball team waits for a game
